cues.text: Watch F1 Finance's accounting machine review October's bills for HANGS Construction. This is accounts payable: money the company owes its suppliers.
First, it reads five files, from the invoices received to the bills in the books. An invoice is simply a supplier's bill.
Next, it matches every invoice to the books. This is called reconciliation. Four mismatches explain the whole $9,532 gap, including one bill entered twice.
An asset is equipment kept for years, and its delivery, setup and tax are part of its cost. Three were booked too low.
Then it checks each bill is charged to the right job and account. Two were not.
Next: is each bill in the right company, approved by the right person, with the vendor's W-9 tax form on file? Four need a different approver.
Last, it writes the workpapers and a draft memo for the controller, the company's head of accounting.

Done. Fifteen findings on 13 of 28 documents, with $69,825 misstated in the books, including a $14,615 bill entered twice, caught before it was paid. Bills worth $90,810 wait for approval. Nothing was posted or paid; a person decides every item.
